actions.action: Slide plant out of pot and inspect roots
Trim rotten roots, mostly black/yellow leaves and mushy stems
Repot in fresh well-draining mix (with perlite/orchid bark if dense) in a pot 1-2 inches wider with drainage
Water thoroughly only after top 1-2 inches of soil dry, checking soil
Empty water from saucer or cachepot
Move plant to bright indirect light away from heaters and drafts
Fertilize lightly in spring and summer after recovery
Switch to filtered or rainwater if tips keep browning

reason: The answer names root rot from overwatering as the main cause, and its root check, trim and repot plan in drainage-friendly mix is an equivalent fix to the water propagation that worked; nothing in it is harmful.
